name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_WAVES_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Wavelength ordering of electromagnetic spectrum waves

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following types of electromagnetic waves in increasing order of their wavelength:
I. Gamma rays
II. Ultraviolet rays
III. Infrared waves
IV. Radio waves

Choose the correct sequence:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electromagnetic waves span a continuous spectrum where each type of wave is characterized by its specific wavelength \(\lambda\) and frequency \(\nu\), related through the fundamental wave equation \(c = \nu \lambda\), where \(c \approx 3 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}\) is the speed of light in vacuum.

Step 2: Analysis of Radiation Wavelengths
According to the classification of the electromagnetic spectrum:
• Gamma rays have the shortest wavelengths, typically less than \(10^{-3}\text{ nm}\) (less than \(10^{-12}\text{ m}\)).
• Ultraviolet rays lie adjacent to the violet end of visible light, with wavelengths extending from about \(400\text{ nm}\) down to \(1\text{ nm}\) (\(4 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}\) to \(1 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}\)).
• Infrared waves lie adjacent to the red end of visible light, with wavelengths extending from \(1\text{ mm}\) down to \(700\text{ nm}\) (\(10^{-3}\text{ m}\) to \(7 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}\)).
• Radio waves have the longest wavelengths in the electromagnetic spectrum, typically exceeding \(0.1\text{ m}\).

Step 3: Determining the Increasing Sequence
Arranging from the smallest wavelength to the largest wavelength gives the order:
Gamma rays \(<\) Ultraviolet rays \(<\) Infrared waves \(<\) Radio waves.
In terms of the given labels, this sequence corresponds to I → II → III → IV.

Final Answer:
The correct increasing sequence of wavelength is Gamma rays → Ultraviolet rays → Infrared waves → Radio waves (I → II → III → IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_WAVES_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Chronological milestones in electromagnetic wave discovery

questiontext.text:
Consider the following historical milestones in the theoretical prediction, laboratory generation, and wireless transmission of electromagnetic waves:
I. Generation and laboratory observation of millimeter-wavelength electromagnetic waves (\(25\text{ mm}\) to \(5\text{ mm}\)) by Jagdish Chandra Bose
II. Theoretical prediction of electromagnetic waves through the formulation of Maxwell's equations and displacement current by James Clerk Maxwell
III. Successful transmission of electromagnetic waves over distances of several kilometres by Guglielmo Marconi
IV. Experimental generation and detection of radio waves in the laboratory by Heinrich Rudolf Hertz

Arrange these milestones in the correct chronological order (from earliest to latest):

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Historical and Conceptual Background
The development of electromagnetic wave theory began with mathematical unification, followed by experimental laboratory verification, and culminated in practical long-distance telecommunications.

Step 2: Evaluation of Milestones and Chronology
• In the 1860s, James Clerk Maxwell unified electricity and magnetism, predicted the existence of electromagnetic waves traveling at the speed of light, and introduced the displacement current.
• In 1887, Heinrich Rudolf Hertz achieved the first laboratory production and detection of electromagnetic waves in the radio frequency range, experimentally confirming Maxwell's prediction.
• Seven years after Hertz's discovery (around 1894–1895), Jagdish Chandra Bose at Calcutta produced and investigated electromagnetic waves of much shorter wavelengths (\(25\text{ mm}\) to \(5\text{ mm}\)) in a laboratory setting.
• Around the same time and following Hertz's work, Guglielmo Marconi succeeded in transmitting electromagnetic waves over open distances of many kilometres, initiating long-range wireless communication.

Step 3: Final Sequence Synthesis
Comparing the chronological dates reveals the proper sequence:
Theoretical prediction by Maxwell (earliest) → Laboratory verification by Hertz → Millimeter-wave generation by J.C. Bose → Long-distance wireless transmission by Marconi (latest).
In terms of the given labels, this sequence is II → IV → I → III.

Final Answer:
The correct chronological order is II → IV → I → III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_WAVES_SEQUENCING_Q03 - Logical deduction sequence of displacement current

questiontext.text:
Maxwell identified an inconsistency in Ampere's circuital law during the charging of a capacitor and resolved it by introducing the displacement current.
Consider the following steps involved in this logical deduction:
I. Differentiating the electric flux through a surface between the plates with respect to time to show that \(\varepsilon_0 \frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_E}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{\mathrm{d}Q}{\mathrm{d}t} = i\)
II. Applying Ampere's circuital law to a flat circular surface outside the plates yielding \(B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 i(t)\), while a pot-shaped surface passing between the plates yields zero current, revealing a contradiction
III. Formulating the generalized Ampere-Maxwell law as \(\oint \mathbf{B} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{l} = \mu_0 i_c + \mu_0 \varepsilon_0 \frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_E}{\mathrm{d}t}\)
IV. Applying Gauss's law to determine the electric field \(E = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0 A}\) and total electric flux \(\Phi_E = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0}\) through a surface between the capacitor plates

Arrange these stages in the correct logical sequence of Maxwell's reasoning:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identifying the Inconsistency in Ampere's Law
Maxwell first evaluated Ampere's circuital law around a loop enclosing the wire leading to a capacitor. Using a flat circular surface bounded by the loop, a conduction current \(i(t)\) passes through, giving \(B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 i(t)\). However, using a pot-like surface sharing the exact same rim but with its body extending between the capacitor plates, no conduction current passes through the surface, giving zero magnetic field. This contradiction showed that Ampere's circuital law was incomplete.

Step 2: Determining Electric Field and Flux Between the Plates
To find what passes through the surface between the plates, the electric field between plates of area \(A\) carrying charge \(Q\) was identified as \(E = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0 A}\). The electric flux through this surface was then evaluated using Gauss's law as \(\Phi_E = E A = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0}\).

Step 3: Relating Time-Varying Flux to Electric Current
As the capacitor charges, the charge \(Q\) varies with time. Differentiating the flux expression gives \(\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_E}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\frac{\mathrm{d}Q}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{i}{\varepsilon_0}\), which directly implies that \(\varepsilon_0 \frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_E}{\mathrm{d}t} = i\), identifying the missing rate of change of electric flux that has the dimensions of current.

Step 4: Formulating the Generalized Ampere-Maxwell Law
Finally, this additional term, called the displacement current \(i_d = \varepsilon_0 \frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_E}{\mathrm{d}t}\), was added to the conduction current \(i_c\). This yielded the Ampere-Maxwell law \(\oint \mathbf{B} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{l} = \mu_0 i_c + \mu_0 \varepsilon_0 \frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_E}{\mathrm{d}t}\), ensuring that the calculated magnetic field remains identical regardless of the surface chosen.

Final Answer:
The correct logical sequence of deduction is II → IV → I → III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_WAVES_SEQUENCING_Q04 - Increasing order of radiation photon energy

questiontext.text:
Consider the electromagnetic radiations utilized in the following practical, medical, and technological applications:
I. Waves used in FM radio broadcast and cellular voice communication
II. Waves emitted by household electronic remote controls and used in physical therapy
III. Waves used in water purifiers to kill germs and in precision LASIK eye surgery
IV. Waves produced during nuclear reactions and emitted by radioactive nuclei to destroy cancer cells

Arrange these electromagnetic radiations in increasing order of their photon energy (\(E = h\nu\)):

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Planck's relation, the energy of a quantum of radiation (photon) is directly proportional to its frequency \(\nu\) and inversely proportional to its wavelength \(\lambda\):
\[E = h\nu = \frac{hc}{\lambda}\]
Therefore, radiation with a lower frequency (or longer wavelength) has lower photon energy, whereas radiation with a higher frequency (or shorter wavelength) has higher photon energy.

Step 2: Identification of Radiations by Application
• FM broadcast and cellular communication operate using Radio waves (\(\nu \sim 10^7\text{ Hz}\) to \(10^9\text{ Hz}\), \(\lambda \sim 10^{-1}\text{ m}\) to \(10^1\text{ m}\)).
• TV remotes and physical therapy utilize Infrared waves (\(\nu \sim 10^{11}\text{ Hz}\) to \(4 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\), \(\lambda \sim 1\text{ mm}\) to \(700\text{ nm}\)).
• Germicidal lamps in water purification and LASIK eye surgery utilize Ultraviolet rays (\(\nu \sim 7.5 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\) to \(3 \times 10^{17}\text{ Hz}\), \(\lambda \sim 400\text{ nm}\) to \(1\text{ nm}\)).
• Destruction of cancer cells via nuclear emissions utilizes Gamma rays (\(\nu > 3 \times 10^{19}\text{ Hz}\), \(\lambda < 10^{-11}\text{ m}\)).

Step 3: Ordering by Increasing Photon Energy
Comparing the frequencies and photon energies gives the progression:
Radio waves (\(E \sim 10^{-7}\text{ eV}\)) < Infrared waves (\(E \sim 10^{-2}\text{ eV}\)) < Ultraviolet rays (\(E \sim 10^1\text{ eV}\)) < Gamma rays (\(E > 10^5\text{ eV}\)).
Thus, the correct sequence in increasing order of photon energy is I → II → III → IV.

Final Answer:
The correct sequence in increasing order of photon energy is Radio waves → Infrared waves → Ultraviolet rays → Gamma rays (I → II → III → IV).
